newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 23.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
RAJASTHAN ASSEMBLY ADJOURNED

The Rajasthan Assembly was adjourned until March 6 after the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party took a vote of confidence, proving its majority on the floor of the House. The ruling party mustered the support of 115 members in a House having current effective strength of 199. Amidst confusion, Speaker Shanti Lal Chaplot gave a ruling suspending five members of the House for three months for unruly behaviour and for stalling the proceedings of the House.
The Economic Times
NO DISTRESS SALE OF PUBLIC SECTOR SHARES

The government would not go for distress sales of shares of public sector enterprises (PSE) just to hit the budget target of mopping up five billion rupees through disinvestment in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said. Unperturbed by the failure of the disinvestment programme in 1995/96 and its delay in taking off this financial year, Maran said the government would wait for markets to improve before divesting PSE shares. The minister also promised concrete measures to improve the lot of PSEs.
ICICI SECURITIES AND FINANCE REVAMP TO TAKE ON RIVALS

ICICI Securities and Finance finalised its restructuring plan. ICICI Securities, the joint venture between Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) and U.S. investment bank JP Morgan, would now have a matrix structure divided between distinct branches of product and relationship groups. These would be individual profit centres functioning as strategic business units. Sources said the revamp was planned to take full advantage of the core competencies which were loosely structured. The step had been taken to improve the business focus of the company to take on the competition in a better way, sources added.
HIGHER WHEAT OUTPUT PROJECTED

The Agriculture Ministry projected a higher rabi (winter) wheat output of 64 million tonnes than last year's 62.5 million tonnes. This was largely due to better reservoir position and encouraging trend in fertiliser and credit uptake by farmers. Sources said while initial reports of widespread rains over the weekend had brightened the crop prospects in rainfed areas, favourable indicators supported a good harvest from irrigated wheat, which was about 95 percent of the total output.
DCM SPIKES DAEWOO PLAN TO HIKE STAKE

The government rejected Daewoo's move to hike its stake to 87 percent in its 6.88 billion rupee joint venture, DCM Daewoo. This followed objections from Daewoo's erstwhile partner, DCM Ltd. The Korean automobile major had sought approval for raising its stake to 87 percent from the existing 75 percent by picking up the unsubscribed portion of the present rights issue. According to the present shareholding pattern, Daewoo holds 75 percent of the equity, DCM group 3.22 percent and the remaining 21.78 percent is with others, including Toyota.
Financial Express
SECURITIES WATCHDOG MAY HAVE A SAY IN MERGERS

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), which rules on takeovers, is likely to have a say in the matters of mergers and amalgamations. At present, these matters are the sole preserve of the Companies Act and the courts. Sources said a move in this direction had been initiated with the SEBI-constituted committee on takeovers discussing the question of acquisitions in the garb of mergers and whether such moves were against the interest of shareholders. They said that while the committee agreed that mergers could be misused. Sources said the involvement of SEBI in mergers and amalgamations could come through mandatory comments from the securities watchdog on proposals to the courts
ESCORTS YAMAHA TAPPING FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS

Escorts Yamaha Motor is negotiating with financial institutions (FIs) and banks for private placement of equity before going public to raise funds for its expansion plans. The the joint venture company planned to raise around 2.5 billion rupees from the public as well as FIs and banks in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). However, the exact size of the issue would depend on private placement with FIs and banks, sources said.
BANKS IN RED AS CORPORATES TURN DEFAULTERS

The industrial slowdown sent the corporate sector crashing towards loan defaults. Many large borrowers failed to keep up interest payments in the first three quarters of the year (April-December, 1996). Sources said this had threatened the bottomlines of banks and other financial intermediaries in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). Even at banks like American Express, the default list in the case of leasing and hire-purchase loans added up to an impressive 256. Sources said in the case of other financial companies, the default lists were even longer.
PUBLIC SECTOR LOSSES INCREASE TO 49.1 BLN RUPEES

The public sector undertakings' (PSUs) losses almost doubled in the post-reform period. The Disinvestment Commission's note on PSUs showed there was a corresponding increase in the number of loss-making units. The number of loss-making units in 1990/91 (April-March) was 96 which went up to 109 in 1995/96. Forty-seven of them fell in the taken-over category accounting for 9.8 billion rupee losses out of the total of 49.1 billion rupees. Making a sectoral analysis, the note said 75 percent of the cumulative losses had been incurred by companies in the manufacturing business.
The Observer
SIEMENS' ISDN PHONE PUT ON HOLD

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) refused to give a green signal to Siemens for selling its Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) phones in the country. Sources said the DoT denied certification to the German multinational on the ground that it failed to furnish the required test reports. DoT had been insisting on a certificate of approval from a German agency, saying its own Telecommunications Engineering Centre was not well equipped to carry out the tests. However, Siemens officials said the company was not in a hurry to get the approval and would get the required certification soon.
MINISTRY SWITCHES OFF PRIME MINISTER'S PROPOSAL

The Power Ministry is not going ahead with the prime minister's proposal for delegating more powers to states for clearing power projects involving investments of over 10 billion rupees. The ministry felt states lacked adequate infrastructure to handle such projects on their own. Furthermore, there was no alternative to the Central Electricity Authority in a state which could study the techno-economic aspects of a mega project. Other vital issues involve fuel linkages, fuel availability, arranging foreign exchange and financing projects, among others.
RESTRICT FOREIGN BROKERS' ENTRY: BROKERS

Representatives of the major stock exchanges, at their meeting with the special parliamentary committee on finance, opposed the entry of foreign share brokers into the country's capital markets. They said an unrestricted entry of the foreign share brokers would virtually wipe out the Indian share brokers from the business. They demanded a clear and long-term policy relating to the foreign brokers' operations in the country. The representatives also proposed measures like relief in the minimum alternative tax, amendment to the Companies Act and the Income Tax Act and revival of forward trading to revive the sagging capital market.
Business Standard
IDBI MUTUAL SET TO LAUNCH FIRST MONEY MARKET FUND

IDBI Mutual Fund is set to launch the country's first money market mutual fund scheme. Sources said IDBI Mutual, which had already received the approval from the Reserve Bank, would launch the scheme by March 31, much ahead of its competitors ABN Amro and the Unit Trust of India. The instruments in which money market mutual fund schemes can invest are treasury bills and dated government securities having an unexpired maturity up to one year, call and notice money, commercial paper, commercial bills accepted/co-accepted by banks and certificate of deposits.
GDP GROWTH RATE FOR 1995-96 ESTIMATED AT 7.1 PCT

India's gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 7.1 percent during fiscal 1995/96 (April-March). The Central Statistical Organisation estimated GDP, at 1980/81 constant prices, at 2,742.09 billion rupees, while at current prices, it put the figure at around 9,557.87 billion rupees. The latest figures should set at rest speculation over what the actual GDP growth rate was in 1995/96, the final year of the Eighth Plan. The 1995/96 Economic Survey had estimated the GDP growth rate at 6.2 percent. But later the Reserve Bank of India had scaled it down to just six percent. Subsequently, the update on the 1995/96 Economic Survey had revised upwards the GDP estimate for last fiscal year at seven percent
Business Line
BSE HIKES LIMIT ON NET CUMULATIVE BUSINESS

In view of the current market situation, the Bombay bourse increased member brokers' limit for net cumulative business in cash shares. The limit was raised to 750,000 rupees, from 500,000 rupees for individual scrips and to five million rupees from four million for gross cumulative business for all scrips.
NORMS FOR FOREIGN AIRLINES

The government announced a 60-day time frame for granting permission to foreign airlines seeking to introduce scheduled flights, among other guidelines. The guidelines, part of an aeronautical information circular and the first-ever norm for international airline operations from India, were issued by the director general of civil aviation. Most of the guidelines have been in existence but were earlier available as thumb rules, official sources said, which international carriers discovered on applying for clearance from different bodies.
